causalModel.founding: A Legion column left unpaid at the recall never marched home; its grandsons keep the roster and the colours.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: A bench on the hill above a junction of two tracks, out of sight of the Gideon road, with the stream's ravine below it for a retreat.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: They keep watches, wear the colours and call what they take a levy.
causalModel.pressures: Gideon will not pay to clear them. The toll company would rather use them.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: Would disband inside a season if Gideon offered them a pardon and a wage.

districts.notes: Four Legion tents in one dressed line on a hillside bench, a fire in front of them and a barricade on the track below.

why.what: The camp: the tent line, its fire and the levy post on the track.
why.whyHere: The column holds a track junction a bend off the Gideon road, where carts for Mile House and the town to the north must pass.
why.whySpot: The one level bench on the hillside above the junction.
why.whyNeighbours: The track bends away to the west and the hill rises to the south-west, so no neighbour sees the tents.
why.playerPurpose: A hostile camp that asks for a levy on the track and will parley before it fights.
why.microGeography: A narrow level bench on a hillside of aspen, the ground falling away to the stream and the track below.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its open long side faces north to the brazier and the track below, at the head of the line.

why.what: The serjeant's command tent, with the campaign table and the pay book on it.
why.whyHere: The column keeps its orders, its roster and its accounts the way the Legion taught it.
why.whySpot: The west end of the bench, at the head of the line.
why.whyNeighbours: The three sleeping tents stand in line beside it; its brazier burns at its mouth.
why.playerPurpose: The serjeant's tent, where the pay book and the toll office's schedules are kept.
why.microGeography: The west end of the bench, on ground levelled for the tent and its brazier.

parcels.worksWithWhy: The command tent heads the line; the first squad's tent stands at its side within call, the spacing Skyrim's Legion camps keep.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its open gable faces north to the line walk, dressed on the command tent.

why.what: The first sleeping tent of the line, next to the serjeant's.
why.whyHere: The column sleeps under issue canvas, a squad to a tent, as it was taught.
why.whySpot: Beside the command tent on the bench, where the ground was levelled first.
why.whyNeighbours: The command tent at the head of the line, the brazier beyond it.
why.playerPurpose: A sleeping tent to search, where the first squad of the column keeps its kit.
why.microGeography: Levelled canvas floor on the bench beside the command tent.

parcels.worksWithWhy: Pitched beside the command tent and the middle tent in one dressed line, as Skyrim's Legion camps pitch theirs (mined line template vanilla:t0224: small tents 4.13 m apart at one yaw).

parcels.orientationWhy: Its open gable faces north, square to the camp path that ends at it.

why.what: The middle sleeping tent, at the head of the camp path.
why.whyHere: A second squad's canvas, pitched to the same line and the same yaw as the first.
why.whySpot: The middle of the bench, where the camp path comes up from the track.
why.whyNeighbours: The tents either side of it, the camp path in front.
why.playerPurpose: A sleeping tent at the head of the camp path, the first one a player reaches.
why.microGeography: Levelled canvas floor in the middle of the line.

parcels.worksWithWhy: The middle of the dressed line, a tent's width from its neighbours on either side, the spacing Skyrim's own Legion camps keep.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its open gable faces north, the last of the line, toward the barricade below.

why.what: The last sleeping tent, at the east end of the line by the banner.
why.whyHere: The third squad's canvas; the line ends here because the bench does.
why.whySpot: The east end of the bench, where the ground starts to fall to the stream.
why.whyNeighbours: The banner stands beyond it; the levy post is below on the track.
why.playerPurpose: The last sleeping tent, nearest the barricade, where the watch sleeps off its turn.
why.microGeography: Levelled canvas floor at the east end of the bench, above the camp path.

parcels.worksWithWhy: The end of the dressed line, pitched at the line's spacing from the middle tent; the bench ends a few steps further east.

routes.why: The trodden way up from the Mile House track to the end of the tent line, the only way into the camp.
The walk along the front of the tent line from the camp path to the mouth of the command tent.
A step off the line walk to the mouth of the first sleeping tent.
A step off the line walk to the mouth of the middle sleeping tent.

occupants.cultureRole: the serjeant, who will parley before he fights
what is left of the column

approaches.sequence: Coming east along the track, the banners show on the hill first, then the tent line, then the barricade across half the track below it.
approaches.wayfinding: The track runs under the bench; a footpath climbs from the barricade to the fire.

approaches.sequence: Coming down the track from the north to the stream, the barricade stands at the junction ahead and the tents above it on the right.
approaches.wayfinding: The junction is at the stream; the barricade is a few steps west of it.

networkTerminals.why: The camp path leaves the Mile House track below the bench, runs east beside it past the barricade and climbs to the end of the tent line.

combatSpaces.why: The trodden ground between the tent line and the fire, the one level footing on the hillside.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: catalogue record The Broke Column (camp, M1): four Legion tents pitched in a line
scaleGrounding.why: One command tent and three sleeping tents hold a serjeant and what is left of a column.

candidates.rejectedBecause: It lies on the stream at the track junction, wet and on the tracks.
